headline: PAGASA Outlook Flags More Cyclones as Strong El Niño Risk Builds Toward Year-End
seoTitle: PAGASA Cyclone Outlook and Strong El Niño Risk for Late 2026 | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA's late-2026 climate outlook warns of additional tropical cyclones while El Niño could strengthen toward very strong levels late in the year.
deck: The approved newsroom brief reports five to seven additional tropical cyclones before year-end as forecasters also monitor the possibility of a very strong El Niño.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA's late-year climate outlook, as reported in the approved FMB News briefing, projects five to seven additional tropical cyclones forming within or entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility before the end of 2026.
The outlook comes as forecasters continue to monitor an El Niño event that could strengthen substantially toward the final months of the year.

sections.heading: El Niño risk
paragraphs: PAGASA has previously said El Niño could intensify from moderate to strong conditions and potentially reach very strong levels late in 2026. The agency has also clarified that 'Super El Niño' is not an official PAGASA classification; very strong El Niño refers to sea-surface temperature anomalies of 2.0 degrees Celsius or higher.

Government climate guidance has warned that rainfall can decline significantly as El Niño strengthens, raising risks for agriculture, water supply and power systems even while individual tropical cyclones can still produce destructive rainfall and flooding.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Philippines can face both drought risk and severe cyclone impacts during the same broad season. El Niño tends to suppress rainfall over many areas, but a passing tropical cyclone can still concentrate extreme rain, wind and storm-surge hazards over affected communities.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The combination requires disaster planning in two directions: maintaining readiness for late-season cyclones while preparing water, food and energy systems for a potentially much drier final quarter and early 2027.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA's succeeding monthly climate assessments will be important for refining the expected number of cyclones and the strength and duration of El Niño. Local governments, utilities and agricultural agencies are expected to adjust preparedness measures as those forecasts become more specific.
